correctness.rationale: In characteristic different from 2 the ordinary bracket equals twice the product of the odd parts, and the top-degree odd part acts trivially. If u∈V is nonzero, replacing one generator of a basis starting with u by the full odd part respects the exterior relations and preserves parity; the associated graded map for the positive-degree filtration is invertible, so this is an automorphism. For u itself, the image on the odd part is u times the odd part of the exterior algebra on a four-dimensional complement; its dimension is 8. If u=0, only the bracket from degrees 3 and 1 can survive. A volume form identifies this map with the alternating form β(v,w)=vol(α∧v∧w); the correspondence from 3-forms to alternating 2-forms is an isomorphism. The possible ranks are 0, 2 and 4; rank-two forms are the nonzero elements of ∧²U with U an arbitrary two-plane of V*, uniquely their image in V*. Counting those forms and the 17 central coordinates gives the stated polynomial. The kernel of the bracket is the centralizer and averaging q^(−r) proves the commuting probability. The reduced rank≤4 locus is u=0; rank≤2 there is the quadratic Plücker cone times the central affine factor. Its punctured cone is a line bundle with zero section removed over the smooth Grassmannian and the vertex has 10-dimensional tangent space but dimension 7. This proves singular locus exactly the center, with the stated dimensions over algebraically closed fields of characteristic not 2. As a bounded check, direct wedge-column rank enumeration over F3 reproduced (1,2420,56628), via python3 /workspace/replay_checks.py 2. The frozen program uses the effective 16×16 block of the 32-dimensional commutator (with zero rows/columns omitted); its partial F5 enumeration is not a general-field or geometric proof.

Five generators exhibit a genuine distinction between decomposable and nondecomposable alternating forms on the zero-linear subspace, alongside the generic rank-eight branch. Identifying the exceptional locus and its singular center provides more than listing a few test-field counts and explains the fiber multiplicities in every odd finite field.
